Orion's Belt.tip: Three bright stars in a short, straight line at Orion's middle. Follow the line down and to the left to reach Sirius.

Big Dipper.tip: Follow the two stars at the far end of the bowl (Merak to Dubhe) upward about 5 fists to find Polaris.

Summer Triangle.tip: High overhead on summer evenings: three bright stars, each in a different constellation, forming a large triangle.

Winter Triangle.tip: Rises with Orion on winter evenings; Sirius, the brightest star in the sky, marks the bottom corner.

Winter Hexagon.tip: A large ring of six bright stars surrounding Orion, visible all through northern winter.

Southern Cross.tip: The smallest constellation in the sky. Its long axis points toward the south celestial pole.

Great Square of Pegasus.tip: A big, nearly empty square rising in autumn evenings. From its upper-left corner you can hop to the Andromeda Galaxy.

Cassiopeia's W.tip: A bright W shape straddling the Milky Way, on the opposite side of Polaris from the Big Dipper.

Teapot.tip: Look low in the south on summer evenings: the Sagittarius stars form a teapot, with the Milky Way rising like steam from its spout.
